notes: 3 evals (add comments / audit planted defects / generate from scratch), 29 assertions: with_skill 29/29, without_skill 24/29 (82.9%). The gain is clearly larger than for python-comments — more of the C++ rules are things the model does not do by default.

Baseline losses: duplicating the header contract in the .cc (the backoff formula appears twice); explanatory comments for standard-library mechanics (try_emplace semantics, erase iterator advancement) that the guide assumes the reader knows; ranking missing contracts (the negative-ttl sentinel) below formatting issues in the audit; missing Get()'s evict-on-read side effect; 'Nothing to acquire'-style restating comments and Python-style Args:/Returns: sections leaking into C++ comments in generated code.

Audit eval: with_skill found all 12 planted defects plus real unplanted extras (missing thread-safety statement, undocumented Evict/notify) and kept the strict wrong -> missing -> placement -> noise ordering; the baseline scored 10/12.
Cost: with_skill spends roughly 6-7k extra tokens per eval and 20-40% more wall time.
Possible next-iteration improvement: plant subtler defects (a comment contradicting a default argument value; an override comment diverged from the base-class contract).
